description: Arc Diagram An Arc Diagram is a powerful and elegant data visualization used to display relationships or connections between entities. It is especially effective when the goal is to identify patterns, clusters, or repeated links within a sequence of nodes. Each node is positioned along a single axis, and relationships between them are illustrated as arcs that connect pairs of nodes. Key Features Minimal and clean layout ideal for spotting patterns. Arcs represent connections, allowing for quick visual correlation. Helps to identify clusters, symmetry, and recurring patterns. Ideal for both directed and undirected relationships. Data Requirements The Arc Diagram requires the following data fields: Dimension 1 (Source Node): The origin of a connection or entity. Dimension 2 (Target Node): The destination or linked entity. Measure: A numeric value representing the strength, frequency, or weight of the relationship between source and target. How It Works Nodes (categories or items from the dimensions) are placed along a linear axis, typically in the order they appear or sorted by a relevant criterion. For every pair of connected nodes, an arc is drawn from the source to the target. The arc's size or thickness may correspond to the numeric measure, conveying the intensity of the connection. Use Cases Network Analysis: Displaying social media connections, email communication paths,…
